intent.raw_query: Mexico City food and culture, $900 solo, 5 days, any month 2026

experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets, sampling exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tacos, and artisanal products. Chat with local vendors and discover ingredients central to Mexican cuisine.

experiences.name: Museo Nacional de Antropología
experiences.description: Visit one of the world's greatest anthropology museums, home to the iconic Aztec Sun Stone and vast collections spanning Mexico's pre-Hispanic civilizations including Maya, Olmec, and Teotihuacan cultures. A must for any culture enthusiast.

experiences.name: Street Taco Crawl in Coyoacán
experiences.description: Wander through the bohemian neighborhood of Coyoacán sampling iconic street foods — al pastor tacos, tlayudas, tamales, and fresh aguas frescas — at local fondas and street stalls beloved by chilangos (Mexico City locals).

experiences.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul)
experiences.description: Tour the iconic Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born and lived, now a museum preserving her personal belongings, artwork, and the vibrant cultural legacy she left behind. A deeply moving cultural and artistic experience.

experiences.name: Cooking Class in Roma Norte
experiences.description: Join a hands-on traditional Mexican cooking class in the trendy Roma Norte neighborhood. Learn to make mole, handmade tortillas, and classic salsas from a local chef, then enjoy the meal you've prepared with fellow travelers.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Benito Juárez International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal Aérea station (very budget-friendly at ~$0.25 USD) or a pre-booked authorized airport taxi to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and rest.

meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night taco from a street stand near the hotel if hungry upon arrival — look for 'tacos de canasta' or 'tacos al pastor' stands open late, typically 20–40 MXN per taco (~$1–2 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Keep pesos handy for metro or small purchases. Exchange currency at the airport or use ATMs (avoid exchange booths with high fees). The Mexico City Metro is the cheapest and fastest way to get around at ~5 MXN per ride.

day_by_day.morning: Start the day at the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world — free to visit. Explore the stunning Catedral Metropolitana (free entry) and admire the Palacio Nacional, which houses Diego Rivera's famous murals (free entry with ID). Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the historic architecture of Centro Histórico.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Templo Mayor archaeological site (entry ~80 MXN / ~$4 USD), the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlán. Visit the adjoining Museo del Templo Mayor to see artifacts and learn about Aztec civilization. Afterward, stroll through the pedestrian street Madero Street, lined with historic buildings and street performers — all free.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Plaza Garibaldi (free entry) to experience mariachi bands performing in the square — a quintessential Mexico City cultural experience. Browse the lively atmosphere and enjoy the energy of the plaza.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local 'fonda' (neighborhood eatery) near the hotel — look for a comida corrida breakfast set with eggs, beans, tortillas, and coffee for around 60–80 MXN (~$3–4 USD).
meals.lunch: Try 'Tacos de Canasta' from street vendors near Centro Histórico — 5 tacos for about 50 MXN (~$2.50 USD). Or visit Mercado de San Juan for affordable local food stalls.
meals.dinner: Dine at a local 'taquería' near Plaza Garibaldi — tacos de barbacoa or carnitas with agua fresca for around 80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD) total.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Centro Histórico is best explored on foot. Most museums in Mexico City offer free entry on Sundays for Mexican residents; foreigners pay a small fee. Keep valuables secure in crowded areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán neighborhood (Line 3 to Viveros station). Visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for a vibrant local market experience — browse fresh produce, crafts, and street food. Then walk to the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) — book tickets in advance online (~270 MXN / ~$13 USD) to avoid long lines. This is one of Mexico City's most beloved cultural sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo in the heart of Coyoacán — free public squares with street artists, vendors, and a relaxed bohemian atmosphere. Visit the Museo León Trotsky nearby (~50 MXN / ~$2.50 USD) for a fascinating historical experience. Wander the colorful colonial streets of Coyoacán at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center via Metro and visit the rooftop terrace of the Palacio de Bellas Artes (exterior and ground floor free) to admire the stunning Art Nouveau architecture illuminated at night. Walk along Avenida Juárez and enjoy the lively street scene.

meals.breakfast: Have 'tostadas de tinga' or 'enfrijoladas' at Mercado de Coyoacán food stalls — around 50–70 MXN (~$2.50–3.50 USD).
meals.lunch: Enjoy a full 'comida corrida' (set lunch menu: soup, main dish, drink, dessert) at a local fonda in Coyoacán for 80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD) — the best budget meal deal in Mexico.
meals.dinner: Try 'tlayudas' or 'memelas' at a street food stall near Bellas Artes or grab tortas from a local 'tortería' for 50–80 MXN (~$2.50–4 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Coyoacán is a must-visit for culture and local food lovers. Pre-book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets online as they sell out fast. The Metro ride from downtown to Coyoacán takes about 25–30 minutes and costs only ~5 MXN.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Teotihuacán, the ancient pre-Columbian city famous for the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon. Take a bus from Terminal Central del Norte (Metro Line 5 to Autobuses del Norte station) — round-trip bus fare ~100 MXN (~$5 USD). Entry to the archaeological zone is ~90 MXN (~$4.50 USD). Climb the Pyramid of the Sun for breathtaking panoramic views and explore the Avenue of the Dead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — visit the Temple of Quetzalcóatl and the Palace of Quetzalpapálotl. Browse artisan vendors near the site for affordable handcrafted souvenirs. Head back to Mexico City by mid-afternoon (buses run frequently).
day_by_day.evening: Relax in the trendy Condesa or Roma neighborhood — stroll through Parque México (free) and admire the Art Deco architecture. Explore the lively street scene, browse local bookshops and boutiques, and enjoy the laid-back vibe of these beloved neighborhoods.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departing — grab 'tamales' and 'atole' (traditional hot corn drink) from a street vendor near the Metro station for about 40–60 MXN (~$2–3 USD).
meals.lunch: Have lunch at one of the small comedores (simple eateries) near the Teotihuacán site entrance — quesadillas, tlacoyos, and agua fresca for around 80–100 MXN (~$4–5 USD).
meals.dinner: Dine at a local taquería in Colonia Roma — try 'tacos de suadero' or 'tacos de costilla' for 15–20 MXN each. A satisfying dinner costs around 80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD).

day_by_day.notes: Start early for Teotihuacán (depart by 8:00–8:30 AM) to avoid afternoon heat and crowds. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water — the site is largely open with minimal shade. The bus from Terminal del Norte to Teotihuacán takes about 1 hour.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bosque de Chapultepec, one of the largest urban parks in the Americas — free entry to the park itself. Explore the stunning Castillo de Chapultepec (entry ~95 MXN / ~$4.75 USD), a hilltop castle with panoramic city views and exhibits on Mexican history. Walk through the park's lakes, gardens, and shaded pathways.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología (entry ~90 MXN / ~$4.50 USD), located within Chapultepec Park — one of the finest anthropology museums in the world, housing the famous Aztec Sun Stone. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the incredible pre-Columbian collections. Afterward, browse the Mercado de Artesanías nearby for affordable souvenirs and handicrafts.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure if needed. For a final farewell dinner, explore a local 'mercado' or street food corridor — enjoy your last tacos, elotes (corn on the cob), and a fresh 'agua de jamaica' (hibiscus water) to wrap up the trip on a delicious budget note.

meals.breakfast: Enjoy 'chilaquiles' (tortilla chips in salsa with cheese and cream) at a nearby fonda or market — a classic Mexican breakfast for 70–100 MXN (~$3.50–5 USD).
meals.lunch: Grab street food within Chapultepec Park or nearby — 'elotes,' 'esquites,' and 'tortas' from vendors for around 60–80 MXN (~$3–4 USD).
meals.dinner: Final dinner at a beloved local taquería or market food stall — try 'pozole' (hominy soup) or 'enchiladas' for a hearty farewell meal at around 80–120 MXN (~$4–6 USD).

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología is free on Sundays for Mexican nationals but has a small fee for international visitors on other days. Chapultepec is perfect for a relaxed final day. Keep Metro cards topped up for easy travel. Overall daily budget estimate: 400–600 MXN (~$20–30 USD) per day including transport, entry fees, and meals.

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late night arrival. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — arrival is at 22:30. Settle into your room and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Once checked in, take a short stroll near the hotel to get oriented, grab a late-night snack from a nearby taqueria or convenience store.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal
meals.dinner: Late-night tacos at a nearby street taco stand or 24-hour taqueria close to the hotel — budget-friendly and authentically Mexican

day_by_day.notes: Flight lands at 22:30. Allow 60–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and transfer to the hotel. Keep Day 1 light — rest is the priority. Confirm hotel has 24-hour check-in. Exchange some currency or use an ATM at the airport for pesos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the historic Centro Histórico — explore the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Walk through the Metropolitan Cathedral and admire its baroque architecture. Stroll to the nearby Templo Mayor archaeological site and museum to learn about the ancient Aztec civilization at the heart of modern Mexico City.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire the stunning art nouveau and art deco architecture and browse the murals by Diego Rivera and other Mexican masters inside. Afterward, walk through Alameda Central Park for a relaxing break. Explore the nearby Mercado de Artesanías or browse local craft shops for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the vibrant Barrio de la Merced or head to a local cantina in Centro Histórico for a traditional Mexican dinner. Experience the lively nighttime atmosphere around the Zócalo, which is often lit up and buzzing with street performers.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try chilaquiles or tamales with café de olla at a local fonda (small family-run eatery)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de San Juan or a nearby comida corrida restaurant — a set meal of soup, main course, and drink for around 80–150 MXN, great mid-range value
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional cantina in Centro Histórico — try classic dishes like mole negro, chiles en nogada, or cochinita pibil with agua fresca or a local craft beer

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Centro Histórico involves a lot of walking on cobblestone streets. The Templo Mayor museum has a small entrance fee (~90 MXN). Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded areas. Metro is a cheap and efficient way to get around (7 MXN per ride).

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to the Floating Gardens of Xochimilco — a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Board a colorful trajinera (flat-bottomed boat) and glide through the ancient canals. Enjoy the festive atmosphere with mariachi musicians and vendors selling food and flowers from their own boats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museo Frida Kahlo (La Casa Azul) in the charming Coyoacán neighborhood. Explore the cobblestone streets, plazas, and colonial architecture of Coyoacán. Browse the Mercado de Artesanías de Coyoacán for handmade crafts, textiles, and local art.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner in Coyoacán — one of Mexico City's most bohemian and culturally rich neighborhoods. Then either return to the hotel or explore the lively Jardín Centenario plaza in the evening, where locals gather and street performers entertain.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Coyoacán before heading to Xochimilco — try molletes (toasted bread with beans and cheese) or fresh fruit with granola
meals.lunch: Snack on food sold by vendors on the trajineras in Xochimilco — elotes (corn), tamales, and quesadillas are popular and affordable options
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Coyoacán — try regional Mexican cuisine such as enchiladas verdes, pozole, or a tasting of regional moles

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets in advance online — they sell out quickly (entry ~270 MXN). Xochimilco is best enjoyed in the morning before crowds arrive. Take an Uber or taxi to Xochimilco (~30–45 min from central areas). Coyoacán is very walkable and safe for tourists.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the ancient pyramids of Teotihuacán, located about 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun (the third-largest pyramid in the world) and the Pyramid of the Moon. Walk the Avenue of the Dead and explore the archaeological zone at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Teotihuacán — visit the Temple of the Feathered Serpent (Quetzalcóatl) and the on-site Teotihuacán Museum. On the way back to the city, stop at a local pulquería or mezcal tasting room to sample traditional Mexican agave-based drinks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mexico City and head to the trendy Condesa or Roma neighborhood for dinner and an evening stroll. These neighborhoods are known for their art deco buildings, tree-lined boulevards, independent bookshops, and excellent restaurant scene.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — aim to leave for Teotihuacán by 8:00 AM to beat the crowds and heat
meals.lunch: Lunch at one of the restaurants near the Teotihuacán site entrance — try a set menu with traditional Mexican dishes like barbacoa, nopales salad, or tlayudas
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Colonia Roma or Condesa — explore modern Mexican cuisine with dishes like duck carnitas tacos, huitlacoche quesadillas, or creative ceviches

day_by_day.notes: Teotihuacán is best visited early morning (opens at 9:00 AM) — bring sunscreen, a hat, and water as there is very little shade. Entry fee is approximately 85 MXN. Take a direct bus from Terminal Central del Norte (Norte Bus Station) or book a guided tour for convenience. The climb up the pyramids is steep — wear sturdy shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the world-renowned Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in Latin America. Explore exhibits on pre-Columbian civilizations including the Aztec, Maya, Olmec, and Toltec cultures. Don't miss the famous Aztec Sun Stone (Sunstone Calendar).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Bosque de Chapultepec (Chapultepec Forest) — one of the largest city parks in the Western Hemisphere. Visit Chapultepec Castle for panoramic views of the city and exhibits on Mexican history. Wind down with a relaxing walk through the park and enjoy the local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final evening in the upscale Polanco neighborhood adjacent to Chapultepec. Browse high-end boutiques on Avenida Presidente Masaryk, enjoy a farewell dinner at a celebrated Mexican restaurant, and soak in the sophisticated side of Mexico City before heading back to the hotel to pack.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Polanco or near the hotel — try a Mexican breakfast spread with huevos rancheros, fresh juices, and pan dulce (sweet bread)
meals.lunch: Lunch inside or near the Museo de Antropología — the museum has a café, or grab a quick bite from a food stand in Chapultepec Park
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a well-regarded mid-range restaurant in Polanco — try contemporary Mexican cuisine or a tasting menu showcasing regional ingredients; pair with a mezcal cocktail or Mexican wine

day_by_day.notes: The Museo Nacional de Antropología entry is approximately 85 MXN and is free on Sundays. Allow at least 3 hours for the museum — it is very large. Chapultepec Castle has a separate entry fee (~85 MXN). Polanco is a safe, upscale area ideal for a relaxed final evening. Confirm your departure logistics and arrange airport transfer in advance.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — late-night arrival. Rest and settle into the Aegean Bliss Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — arrival is at 22:30. Transfer from airport to hotel via private luxury car service.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Mexico City International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Meet your private chauffeur for a seamless transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, enjoy a welcome amenity, and unwind with a nightcap at the hotel's rooftop bar overlooking the city skyline.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or pre-departure meal
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in-flight or pre-departure meal
meals.dinner: Late-night light bites and cocktails at the Aegean Bliss Resort rooftop bar — charcuterie boards, artisan cheeses, and premium Mexican spirits such as aged mezcal from Oaxaca

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport private transfer in advance. Confirm early check-in or luggage storage if needed. Keep Day 1 light — the focus is rest after a long flight. Tip: ask the concierge to prepare a personalized itinerary briefing for the morning.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the day with a lavish breakfast at the hotel, then embark on a private guided tour of the Historic Center (Centro Histórico). Visit the magnificent Zócalo — one of the largest public squares in the world — followed by an exclusive guided tour of the Metropolitan Cathedral and the ancient Aztec ruins of Templo Mayor, with a private archaeologist to provide deep cultural context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Palacio de Bellas Artes with a private docent, admiring its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture and world-class murals by Diego Rivera and David Alfaro Siqueiros. Stroll through the Alameda Central park before heading to the iconic Mercado de San Juan for a curated premium tasting experience of artisan cheeses, imported delicacies, and local Mexican ingredients.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a world-class dinner at Pujol, one of Latin America's top-ranked restaurants, helmed by Chef Enrique Olvera. Experience the legendary Mole Madre tasting menu, a celebration of Mexican culinary heritage. Reserve well in advance through the hotel concierge.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — eggs Benedict, fresh tropical fruits, Mexican pastries (conchas, cuernos), freshly squeezed juices, and specialty Veracruz coffee
meals.lunch: Premium tasting experience at Mercado de San Juan — artisan cheeses, cured meats, fresh ceviche, and craft beverages
meals.dinner: Pujol Restaurant — multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing; signature dishes include Mole Madre and Nixtamal corn tostadas

day_by_day.notes: Book Pujol at least 4–6 weeks in advance as it is one of the most sought-after reservations in Mexico City. Wear smart-casual attire for dinner. Private guided tours can be arranged through the hotel concierge for a fully personalized experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private chauffeured drive to the ancient Aztec city of Teotihuacán, located approximately 50 km northeast of Mexico City. Enjoy an exclusive sunrise or early-morning private tour of the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon before the crowds arrive. Optionally, arrange a hot air balloon flight over the archaeological zone for a breathtaking aerial perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City and head to the upscale neighborhood of Polanco for an afternoon of luxury exploration. Visit the world-renowned Museo Soumaya, home to over 66,000 works of art including pieces by Rodin, Dalí, and Rivera — free entry. Browse the designer boutiques along Avenida Presidente Masaryk, Mexico City's answer to the Champs-Élysées.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Quintonil, another of Mexico City's elite restaurants, run by Chef Jorge Vallejo. The menu celebrates contemporary Mexican cuisine using indigenous ingredients and traditional techniques. Follow dinner with craft cocktails at a sophisticated mezcalería in Polanco.

meals.breakfast: Early gourmet picnic breakfast prepared by the hotel and enjoyed at Teotihuacán at sunrise — smoked salmon croissants, fresh fruit, Thermos of premium Mexican coffee
meals.lunch: Elegant lunch at a traditional hacienda-style restaurant near Teotihuacán — lamb barbacoa, handmade tortillas, and regional pulque or craft beer
meals.dinner: Quintonil Restaurant — contemporary tasting menu with Mexican wine or mezcal pairing; highlights include hoja santa with seafood and seasonal vegetable dishes

day_by_day.notes: Hot air balloon flights over Teotihuacán should be booked in advance (recommended operator: Globos Aeroestáticos). Dress in layers for the early morning — temperatures can be cool at sunrise. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the pyramids.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a culturally rich morning in the bohemian neighborhood of Coyoacán. Visit the iconic Museo Frida Kahlo (Casa Azul) with a private guide for an intimate look into the life and art of Mexico's most celebrated painter. Wander through Coyoacán's charming colonial streets, colorful markets, and artisan craft stalls at the Mercado de Artesanías.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the trendy Roma and Condesa neighborhoods for an afternoon of curated cultural exploration. Visit independent art galleries, explore the lush tree-lined boulevards of Parque México, and indulge in a private mezcal or tequila tasting at a premium spirits boutique. Consider a visit to the Museo del Objeto del Objeto (MODO) for a unique look at Mexican design history.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a private chef's table dinner at Rosetta, Chef Elena Reygadas's celebrated restaurant in Roma Norte, known for blending Italian culinary traditions with Mexican ingredients. The intimate ambiance and exceptional wine list make it one of the city's most memorable dining experiences.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at a charming café in Coyoacán — chilaquiles rojos, freshly baked pan dulce, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at a Roma Norte bistro — avocado tostadas, grilled octopus, and a glass of natural Mexican wine
meals.dinner: Rosetta Restaurant — seasonal Italian-Mexican fusion tasting menu with curated wine pairing; signature house-baked breads and handmade pasta

day_by_day.notes: Book Museo Frida Kahlo tickets well in advance as they sell out quickly. Private guide arrangements can be made through the hotel concierge. The Roma and Condesa neighborhoods are best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. Request a chef's table reservation at Rosetta for the most exclusive experience.

day_by_day.morning: Begin your final full day with a private cooking class led by a renowned Mexico City chef. Learn to prepare traditional dishes such as mole negro, tamales, and chiles en nogada using fresh ingredients sourced from a morning visit to a local market. This immersive experience offers deep insight into Mexico's culinary heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Chapultepec Park — one of the largest urban parks in the Western Hemisphere — for a relaxing and culturally rich afternoon. Explore the world-class Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) with a private guide, home to the famous Aztec Sun Stone and extraordinary pre-Columbian collections. Stroll through the park's beautiful gardens and lakeside paths.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate your final evening in Mexico City with a spectacular farewell dinner at Biko, a Basque-Mexican fusion restaurant in Polanco helmed by Michelin-pedigree chefs Bruno Oteiza and Mikel Alonso. Conclude the evening with a private mezcal tasting flight back at the Aegean Bliss Resort rooftop bar, toasting to an unforgettable trip.

meals.breakfast: Included as part of the cooking class experience — freshly prepared traditional Mexican breakfast dishes made during the class, including enfrijoladas and atole
meals.lunch: Light gourmet lunch at the Museo Nacional de Antropología's café or a nearby Polanco restaurant — ceviche, aguachile, and fresh agua fresca
meals.dinner: Biko Restaurant — avant-garde Basque-Mexican tasting menu with premium wine pairing; highlights include creative interpretations of classic Mexican and Basque flavors

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure logistics with the hotel concierge — arrange a private luxury transfer for the return to the airport if departing on Day 6. Purchase any artisan souvenirs or premium spirits (mezcal, tequila) during the market visit in the morning. The cooking class can be arranged through the hotel or a reputable culinary tour operator such as Eat Mexico.
